messages.author: 9ea95ff2561a8857
messages.subject: SEPARABLE for matrix Normal likelihood
parts:
Hello,

I am ultimately trying to use TMB to fit multivariate linear mixed models. They are based on the n x p matrix Normal distribution with two covariance matrices, one between rows (U is n x n) and one between columns (V is p x p) which is the one of interest here. Such a distribution can be re-written as a np multivariate Normal which np x np covariance matrix Sigma is equal to the kronecker product V \otimes U. Because of this, I am trying to use SEPARABLE as I guess it is efficient for such a use case. I hence started to explore this on a small example where p = 2, U is the identity matrix, and V is specified using VECSCALE and UNSTRUCTURED_CORR. However, I can't make it work: any help is much welcomed!

Compilation works well, but I get a "Process R aborted (core dumped)" error when running MakeADFun() with the following details:
TMB has received an error from Eigen. The following condition was not met:
aLhs.rows() == aRhs.rows() && aLhs.cols() == aRhs.cols()
Please check your matrix-vector bounds etc., or run your program through a debugger.

I used the R debugger and I managed to find that the error occurs when h the variable defined as SEPARABLE is being evaluated, even though the argument to h has correct dimensions (I checked with gdb, see "manip_debug.R" below).

Attached you can find:
  • test_debug.R: simulates the data, compiles the cpp code, run MakeADFun and nlminb
  • test_debug.cpp: implements the negative log-likelihood (includes debug_print.hpp)
  • manip_debug.R: use gdbsource() on "test_debug.R" and try to find the cause of the error
Thanks in advance!
TF

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: SEPARABLE for matrix Normal likelihood
parts:
The problem is in

X - M.array()

where X is a tmbutils::array while M.array() is an Eigen::Array.
These array kinds are not the same (TMB arrays are essentially vectors with a dim attribute while Eigen Arrays are restricted to 2D).
Simple fix:

X - M.vec()
